q7.answer: Nowhere as a counter. Each evaluation is a row in the evaluations table, keyed (service, rule, minute_ts), with breaching and healthy flags, and the streak is computed from the latest rows each time. 3 consecutive breaching rows open an incident and 10 consecutive healthy rows resolve it. A missing minute, or a minute that is not breaching (for the open streak) or not healthy (for the resolve streak), breaks the run.

q8.answer: Both instances try to insert the evaluations row for (service, rule, T) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, and only the one whose insert succeeds processes that minute. The other waits, hits the conflict and skips. A unique partial index on incidents (service, rule) WHERE status <> 'resolved' is a second guard against two unresolved incidents.

q9.answer: A sweeper on both instances runs every 10 s and selects open, unacknowledged incidents below level 3 whose stored next_escalation_at has passed. It claims one with a compare-and-set UPDATE that bumps level and moves the deadline forward by 5 min, in the same transaction as inserting the new page row. Only the instance whose update changes a row creates the page. The unique index on (incident_id, level) also stops a level being paged twice.

q10.answer: The provider calls our signature-checked webhook, which runs a CAS UPDATE setting acked_at and acked_by WHERE status = 'open' AND acked_at IS NULL. The sweeper's claim condition requires acked_at IS NULL, so no further level can be claimed. A page claimed at the same instant as the ack may still go out, which is accepted.

q11.answer: At send time. The dispatcher looks up the role for the page's level in the on-call service when it sends the page row, not when the incident opens, so a 09:00 handover mid-incident is picked up. It then stores the resolved person on the page row.

q12.answer: It reads the pages table. When the incident resolves, one resolved-notice row is queued for each distinct recipient already stored on that incident's page rows. This means the people actually paged, not whoever is on call now. A unique index on (incident_id, recipient) for kind = 'resolved' prevents duplicate notices.
